name: Actionable, source-linked error communication
summary: When an error is detected, identify the affected field in text, explain the failure and known safe correction, and connect any summary and detail to the affected answer.
problem: A visual invalid state or unlinked generic message can leave users unable to identify the failed field or correction route.
context: Forms where inputs are automatically validated, especially longer forms with multiple possible errors.
observed_solution: Render specific textual error near affected control/group, programmatically associate it where appropriate, and provide a navigable error overview when the workflow merits it; determine focus behavior from actual task context.
rationale: WCAG 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 (O06/O08), WAI overall/inline notifications (O17), GOV.UK error wording and summary linking/focus convention (O19/O20), Primer label/validation IDs and aria-invalid source (O37/O39/O40). Summary-per-error and focus-to-summary belong to GOV service practice, not all WCAG-conformant forms. Direct behavior of AT untested.
tradeoffs: An error summary may be redundant for a one-field form.
Automatically moving focus can disrupt some workflows.
Suggestions must not reveal information that undermines security/purpose.
applicability: Detectable input errors with known safe correction guidance.
Multi-field workflows where users benefit from an error overview.
non_applicability: Backend outage, eligibility denial or unrelated processing failure that is not a field error.
No automatic error detected; no universal requirement to manufacture an error state.
accessibility_implications: WCAG text error identification and suggestion limits apply; verify actual programmatic associations and focus behavior with AT tests later.
responsive_implications: Keep nearby error and summary-linked target discoverable when regions reflow; preserve routes per W04 accepted knowledge.
implementation_notes: No global error-summary mandate and no one-size-fits-all focus destination.
Do not infer test PASS from pinned aria-invalid code.
GOV.UK's summary link wording consistency is a first-party component convention.

counterexamples.summary: An isolated field with a clearly associated corrective message may not need a second whole-page error overview outside GOV.UK service-specific guidance.
counterexamples.context: Single-field filter or small scoped form.
